“Robyn has been diagnosed with breast cancer. Terrible news,” a statement on her GoFundMe page read. “The good news – she has a crack team at the hospital organizing and planning her surgery and aftercare and recovery.”

Coffin set up the fundraising page with friend Gianine DeFrancesco in hopes of supporting the actress through her upcoming operation and recovery. An initial fundraising goal has been set at $75,000, with more than $15,000 already raised as of publication.

items.summary:
Dakota Mortensen is suing Hulu and the production companies involved in the popular reality TV series The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives for alleged defamation.

“The knowingly false portrayal of Mortensen as the abuser in the relationship continued uninterrupted, while the only footage of physical aggression between the two, aggression by Paul against Mortensen, was intentionally withheld from viewers to promote a false narrative,” Mortensen, 33, reportedly alleged in court documents filed on Friday, November 13, and obtained by ABC 4 read. “The series across seasons 3, 4 and 5 presented Mortensen to millions of viewers as a domestic abuser, as a man who retaliated against the mother of his child by reporting her to child protective services and as a serial adulterer.”

Mortensen dated show star Taylor Frankie Paul on and off during the first five seasons of the Hulu series. The exes, who welcomed son Ever in March 2024, split for good in fall 2025 when Paul, 32, went to film The Bachelorette season 22.

Paul’s season was ultimately pulled days before its March premiere after footage footage of her 2023 arrest for domestic violence resurfaced, showing the influencer hitting and throwing chairs at her ex in the presence of her children. (Paul pleaded guilty to aggravated assault in exchange for the dismissal of additional charges pertaining to child abuse. She completed her three-year probation earlier this year.)

items.title: Joe Jonas' Dating History Through the Years
items.summary:
Joe Jonas ‘ love life has made headlines over the years as he navigated dating in the public eye.

Shortly after the musician started dating Taylor Swift in 2008, their messy split became a topic of conversation. Following three months together, the Pennsylvania native revealed that Jonas broke up with her in a 27-second phone call. 

“It’s all right – I’m cool. “You know what, it’s like, when I find that person that is right for me, he’ll be wonderful,” Swift said while appearing on The Ellen DeGeneres Show in November 2009. “When I look at that person, I’m not even going to remember the boy who broke up with me over the phone in 25 seconds when I was 18. I looked at the call long — it was, like, 27 seconds. That’s got to be a record.”

Jonas found love again with Sophie Turner after they sparked romance rumors in 2016. Following one year of dating, Jonas and Turner announced that they were engaged. The duo secretly tied the knot in May 2019 at a Las Vegas wedding chapel and held a second ceremony in Sarrians, France, one month later.

After welcoming two daughters together, Us Weekly confirmed that Jonas filed for divorce from Turner in September 2023. The proceedings were finalized the next year.

“I have to get a hip replacement — I do,” the Saved by the Bell alum, 52, said on the Tuesday, November 10, episode of Tom Papa ’s eponymous podcast . “I was a dancer when I was younger, which was a good thing, [and] I have a torn labrum, that’s one issue I have. Hip dysplasia, according to the Cleveland Clinic, occurs when bones in the hip joint no longer properly fit together.

“So, when I was very flexible as a young child has now caused my issue now,” she quipped. “I  hear the hip replacements aren’t as bad as knee and shoulders [replacement procedures].”

“We play [as a family],” the actress, who shares two kids with husband Brady Smith , added. “My doctor didn’t say it was pickleball, but it probably is not help[ful]. I have not been able to play in the last couple weeks ‘cause my hip’s been so bad.”

Theissen has also recently been splitting her time between California and Vancouver, Canada, while filming her new show, Disney+’s Coven Academy. 

“It’s a great city. I am in the same time zone so that’s helpful for my family, and it’s an easy flight so I try to come home. I never go more than two weeks without seeing my family,” she said of working in the Canadian…

Another panellist, the TV presenter Dermot O’Leary, mimed picking up a phone and said: “When you’re dancing tonight, do you mind having sex afterwards?” Everyone laughed.

items.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
items.summary:
After years of celebrity interviews, I have learned not to be fooled by the allure of fame. We never really know them – we know what they want us to know

As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.

I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.

Continue reading...
items.t: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood

items.title: Two courtrooms, one celebrity: how did the Russell Brand case compare with the rape trial next door?
items.summary:
One was a high-profile defendant watched by more than 100 journalists. Another was an unknown man who preyed on a girl almost half his age. Their stories played out minutes apart, one entirely out of the spotlight

What is going on inside Russell Brand’s head as he arrives at court for the start of his rape trial? He sees the dozens of cameras and journalists lined outside Southwark crown court, many of whom have been waiting since before 7am, and he tells himself that the media are all against him. “It seems to me that they believe that I am guilty, and that this should be the rubber-stamping of the process of my destruction.”

He walks with his wife, Laura, and his bodyguard past the photographers, “clickering, clackering, snickering paparazzi, like locusts, peculiar concoctions, not fully humans”, and up into the court, where he is suddenly overwhelmed by “the presence of something very beautiful, grace”. “In a situation like I’m in, it’s impossible not to turn to God. Truth and justice are the only things that can save me,” he thinks.
